newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS WINS 16TH, CARTER HITS 10TH SLAM IN JAYS' ROUT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS WINS 16TH, CARTER HITS 10TH SLAM IN JAYS' ROUT.

text.p: Roger Clemens threw eight scoreless innings for his major-league leading 16th win and Joe Carter belted his 10th career grand slam in the Toronto Blue Jays' 8-0 rout of the Milwaukee Brewers Wednesday.

Clemens (16-3), who has won his last four starts, scattered eight hits with two walks and seven strikeouts, lowering his earned run average to a major-league best 1.54. He has allowed two runs or less in 17 of his 21 starts.

After emergency starter Jamie McAndrew walked the first five batters in the fourth inning, Carter greeted reliever Joel Adamson with his second grand slam of the season to extend the Blue Jays' advantage to 7-0.
"The other guy (McAndrew) put a lot of guys on base," Clemens said, "and we were able to take advantage of it. Once Joe hit the grand slam, you just have to go to work and keep putting up zeroes."
"When the bases are loaded, you want to get a grand slam," Carter said. "I wasn't thinking about that, but I got a slider down and in, I hit it like a golf swing and let the wind play with it."
The homer was the 370th of Carter's career, tying him with Gil Hodges for 38th on the all-time list.
McAndrew (1-1), starting in place of Jeff D'Amico, surrendered six runs and just one hit over 3 1/3 innings. D'Amico was out with mild tendinitis in his right shoulder.

In New York, Chad Curtis led off the bottom of the ninth with a double and scored the winning run on a throwing error by second baseman Luis Alicea over the head of pitcher Shigetoshi Hasegawa (2-5), who was covering first on a Jorge Posada grounder, as the Yankees edged the Anaheim Angels 5-4.
"It just got away, I threw it away," Alicea said.
"We were lucky to win this game," Yankees manager Joe Torre said.

Jeff Nelson (3-5) pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings for the win as the Yankees won in their final at-bat for the 12th time this season. Nelson has retired the last 22 batters he has faced, spanning seven appearances.

New York has won seven of its last nine games. Anaheim, which had won 12 of 13 games before dropping the first two games of this series, fell four games behind New York in the American League wild-card race.

At Texas, Jeff Reboulet singled home Geronimo Berroa in the top of the 12th against Danny Patterson (6-4) and the Baltimore bullpen pitched four scoreless innings as the Orioles completed a three-game sweep of the Texas Rangers 3-2.
Randy Myers (2-3) worked two scoreless innings for the victory.
The Orioles, who have won seven of eight meetings with the Rangers this season, stayed 3 1/2 games ahead of the second-place Yankees in the American League East.
Texas, which left 12 men on base, has lost eight of its last 10 contests.
Rafael Palmeiro hit a solo homer for Baltimore in the first while Lee Stevens did the same for Texas in the fifth.

In Boston, Scott Brosius homered and drove in two runs and emergency starter Don Wengert won for the first time in more than a month as the sputtering Oakland Athletics beat the Red Sox 5-2, snapping a four-game losing streak.
The triumph also ended the Athletics' eight-game slide at Fenway Park, where they had not won since May 18, 1996.
Wengert (5-9) got the start after Steve Wojciechowski irritated his left ulnar nerve while warming up.
Tim Wakefield (4-11) took the loss.

In Cleveland, Omar Olivares allowed one earned run over 6 2/3 innings for his first win in over a month and Joey Cora had three hits and scored twice to lead the Seattle Mariners to a 6-3 victory over the Indians.

Olivares (6-6) gave up seven hits, walked three and struck out three in his first start since being acquired from the Tigers on July 18. Olivares, who pitched a three-hit shutout against the Indians for Detroit on May 10, won for the first time since tossing a four-hitter against Florida on June 18.
Former Indian Paul Sorrento homered for Seattle.
In Detroit, Willie Blair overcame a shaky start and Matt Walbeck's two-run homer capped a six-run third inning as the Tigers beat the Chicago White Sox 8-6.

Blair (9-4) was pounded for four runs in the second but wound up giving up five runs and nine hits with no walks and three strikeouts in seven innings. After dropping consecutive outings in mid-June, Blair is 4-0 in five starts and gained a victory in relief against Baltimore on July 6.
The right-hander's five straight wins are the most for a Tiger since David Wells won nine in a row in 1995.
Todd Jones gave up a run in the ninth but notched his career-high 18th save. Detroit has won four of its last six games overall and five of six at home.

At Minnesota, Tim Belcher allowed one run over seven innings for his first win in more than a month and Jay Bell's two-run single capped a four-run second as the Kansas City Royals ended the Twins' five-game winning streak 5-1.
Belcher (9-9) snapped a personal three-game losing streak.
